newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIAN INDUSTRIALISTS URGE TAX INCENTIVES.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIAN INDUSTRIALISTS URGE TAX INCENTIVES.

text.p: The Bulgarian Industry Union (BIU) urged authorities to boost declining production through customs duty and tax breaks in a draft bill submitted to parliament for approval, BIU chairman said.
"We have proposed to parliament to lift customs duties on imported technologies and equipment and reduce or abolish corporate tax on investments," BIU chairman Krastyo Stanilov said.
Currently corporate tax in Bulgaria is 26 percent for a profit up to two million levs and 36 percent for a profit over that amount.
Pending introduction of a restrictive monetary mechanism and steps to speed up privatisation were not enough to increase investor interest unless there were more tax incentives, said Stanilov.

The new reformist Bulgarian cabinet which took office on May 21 pledged to speed up structural reform and introduce a fixed rate exchange regime called a currency board system to stabilise the economy and the fragile lev currency.

"We expect high interest by potential investors as speculation on the local foreign exchange market will not be as profitable under a currency board system as before and parliament should stimulate investors by a liberal tax system", Stanilov said.
The BIU was set up in 1990 by Bulgarian private and state industrial firms.
Bulgarian year on year industrial output fell a real 15.4 percent in the first quarter of 1997 due to the shrinking demand, soaring inflation and the sharp lev fall against the dollar and high rates.

Political instability and delayed reforms triggered first quarter cumulative consumer price inflation to 452 percent and March inflation was 2,040.5 percent. Producer prices rose 2,072.7 percent year on year in March. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
